correctness.rationale: The beta integral for b_{j+1}-b_j yields positive Hausdorff increments. D=(1-u)F has an imaginary part strictly sign-matched to Im u and increases along the negative real axis, proving exact zero count and boundary equality. The canonical space is equivalent to Bergman under coefficient sub-sampling and the divided Blaschke multiplier has codimension-one closed range; boundary cyclicity follows from vanishing monomial norm. Uniform Stirling/differentiated error yields J=2 k^epsilon eta(-epsilon)/Gamma(1+epsilon)-1+O(k^(epsilon-1)), hence the unique crossover and precise constant pi exp(-gamma)/2. Reproducible finite numerical checks are supplementary.
